Hi Ana,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Primary use case: localized product descriptions + assisted search in EU (DE, FR, ES, PL) and APAC (KO, JA).
- Key constraints: GDPR/data residency for EU, low-latency under 300ms p95 for search completions, and strict quality floor for brand voice.
- Success metrics: human acceptance >= 92% on locale QA tests; automated intent/slot accuracy >= 95% for search intent; chrF/BLEU for localized snippets as internal baseline.

Immediate next steps (proposal):
1) We'll run a 2-week model-fit evaluation across a shortlist of models (see attachments) using your sample data.
2) Redwood will provide: benchmark report, per-locale prompt sets, and a suggested production config (batching + quantization profile).
3) Schedule kickoff: proposed Wed 18 May 2026, 9:00 AM CEST.
4) Procurement: if you can share PO cadence/contact, we'll include an estimated scope & cost for the evaluation.

Attached: redwood-multilingual-benchmarks-2026.xlsx (summary of our baseline results), prompt-sets-eu-apac.jsonl (example prompts).

Model shortlist (preliminary): rw-mt-13B, rw-mt-7B-quant, open-mt-7B, rw-lexa-13B (lower-cost baseline). Neha will follow up with evaluation metrics and a reproducible harness.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the final language list and whether any translations are handled in-house vs. user-generated?
- Any hard restrictions on sending masked sample product descriptions outside EU?

Thanks — I'll hold Wednesday 9:00 CEST as tentative.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Hi Ana / Marissa,

Quick technical note from the eval team based on the languages and requirements:
1) Recommended shortlist and why:
   - rw-mt-13B: best overall quality for EU locales, higher token costs but stronger brand-voice fidelity.
   - rw-mt-7B-quant: good latency/cost tradeoff, quantized variant reduces memory footprint on Dedicated pools.
   - open-mt-7B: baseline open model to check value delta and detect hallucination patterns.

2) Evaluation plan & regression handling:
   - Automated pipeline: token-level metrics (chrF, BLEU), intent/slot accuracy, and a human-rated acceptance score (1-5). We run per-locale A/B against your baseline.
   - Regression guardrail: we can configure thresholds (e.g., >3% drop in human acceptance or >5% lift in hallucination rate) to flag automatic rollback. The pipeline will produce per-batch alerts and a single-line JSON report; we can wire that to your Slack/HubSpot.
   - Fallback policy: for production we recommend a tiered fallback: rw-mt-7B-quant (fast) as primary, with rw-mt-13B as fallback for high-confidence prompts, plus an emergency fallback to an earlier pinned model if degradations detected.

3) Data handling & residency:
   - For the eval, masked product descriptions are fine. If you need processing in EU-only infra, we can run the evaluation on our EU Dedicated cluster (additional cost; estimate in attached SLA-draft-Redwood.docx).

4) Artifacts we'll deliver:
   - Benchmark spreadsheet (attached), per-locale prompt-sets (attached), and the eval harness (link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/eval-harness-multilingual).

5) Ask from Globex: please provide a 1k-sample set per locale (masked) and a short list of 15 critical prompts for brand-voice checks.

I'll start the baseline runs once we have the samples and confirmation on EU-only execution.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
